source.title: Optimal learning rate schedules in high-dimensional non-convex optimization problems
source.authors: Stéphane d'Ascoli; Maria Refinetti; G. Biroli

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own learning-rate schedule experiments on teacher-student neural-network regression, a different task and measure from the claim’s classification-error benchmarks. It also analyzes non-convex optimization in theoretical models.
record.gate_note: The neural-network results measure mean-squared regression loss, not training classification error on CIFAR. Other numeric results are from Langevin dynamics on theoretical spin-glass and signal-recovery models. Cited results about other learning-rate work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests learning-rate decay schedules, but none of V1–V6. Its regression experiments do not measure CIFAR classification error, width-dependent spurious-minimum frequency, depth, initialization or normalization effects. Neither these experiments nor its Langevin curvature analyses test recovery above a discrete-time stability limit or edge-of-stability training.
record.authors_conclusion: The record correctly summarizes the neural-network experiment but omits the main theoretical conclusions: optimal decay exponents are 0.4–0.5 in the studied purely non-convex landscapes, whereas signal-recovery problems favor keeping a large constant learning rate during search and decaying after entering an attraction basin. Teacher-student SGD experiments show similar timing dependence. These results do not establish any listed claim version.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Langevin dynamics in theoretical spherical models and SGD in teacher-student regression; reports regression loss rather than benchmark classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: In teacher-student regression, the result depends on when decay begins: decay before the crossover or loss plateau leaves high loss, while decay afterward enables lower loss.

fits_no_version.finding: With batch-size-one SGD and K=M equal to 2, 5 or 20, decay before the crossover leaves high regression loss; decay after the plateau enables lower loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested teacher-student regression networks, keeping the learning rate constant through the search phase and decaying afterward improves convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: The optimal power-law decay exponent is 1/2 in the spherical SK model and 2/5 in the tested p-spin models. Signal-recovery models instead favor a constant learning rate during search followed by inverse-time decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal learning-rate schedules depend on landscape structure and on whether optimization has entered a signal-associated attraction basin.

record.problems: The neural-network experiment is a teacher-student regression task with mini-batch size 1, not a classification benchmark. Exact numeric values for the plotted losses are not stated in the text; uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted; the remaining reported neural-network size conditions are included in R2 and R3. The theoretical spin-glass and signal-recovery experiments do not measure the classification-error behavior named by any version.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional CIFAR classification training error, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe qualifications.

All parts: spurious local-minimum frequency in ReLU teacher-student networks and its reduction with extra student neurons. Equal teacher/student widths across separate schedule experiments do not test this.
All parts: depth degradation, identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh training and normalization-free residual training.
All parts: activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and trainable depth.
All parts: initial stability thresholds, catapult loss and curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training and divergence below the initial threshold.
All parts: batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6, not because the schedule effects are unreadable. V2 concerns regression-compatible teacher-student optimization, not specifically classification as the record suggests. The theoretical results were explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, network size, optimizer comparisons, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student classification and spurious local minima versus student and teacher widths.
Plain versus residual convolutional classification networks, depth effects, shortcuts, Fixup, and deep tanh networks.
Activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and deep plain-network trainability.
Learning rates above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence under full-batch training.
Batch normalization comparisons for training speed, accuracy, or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.size_stated: K = 2 hidden units; teacher M = 2 hidden units; N = 500; P = 10^4
rows.operation_detail: Kept learning rate constant until switch time ts, then decayed as η0/(t−ts)^−β; measured whole-training-set mse.
rows.measure: Mean-squared error on the whole training set over time
rows.value: Decaying after the crossover enables convergence to lower loss; the figure shows schedules with various ts.
rows.note: Authors state that decaying before the crossover leaves optimization stuck at high mse, while decaying after it enables lower loss; the plotted conditions vary ts.
rows.check: The schedule-dependent regression result is valid but measures no listed version. Correct the intended decay formula to η0/(t−ts)^β; the negative exponent in the prose is inconsistent with decay and Figure 5. Separate early and late switch conditions, which produce different outcomes. Figure 7's caption describes convergence to zero loss, while the prose states lower loss; no exact endpoint is supplied.

source_check.correct: The intended decay schedule is η0/(t−ts)^β, with β=0.8 and η0=10^-1. The negative denominator exponent reproduces a source typo and mathematically gives growth.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4, pp. 10–11, Figure 7; Section 3.1, Figure 5 caption explicitly gives the positive denominator exponent.
source_check.problem: The operation describes decay using a formula that increases the learning rate.

relation.reason: It discusses learning-rate instability and related optimization research, but its own results address decay timing and exponents rather than any listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study measures learning-rate scheduling in spherical Langevin models and teacher-student regression. It neither tests nor uses the specific findings in V1–V6; its curvature analysis does not test stability-threshold recovery.

source_check.notes: Figures 7 and 10 list β=0.8, although their captions describe inverse-time decay and zero loss. The surrounding paragraphs support the recorded qualitative lower-loss results; no precise plotted loss values are asserted.
